editorial_candidates.source_claim: The experiment is indexed by the binary hypercube, with target aω; the proof pairs each vertex having bit i=0 with its unique bit-flipped neighbor and bounds the sum of the two testing errors by 1−v (lines 33–42 and 60–63).
editorial_candidates.why_warranted: A small square schematic can make the coordinatewise neighbor pairing behind the risk bound visible.
editorial_candidates.content_to_draw_or_check: Draw a clearly illustrative d=2 square with vertices labelled ω∈{0,1}² and targets tω=aω. Highlight one edge joining ω with ω_i=0 to ω^(i), label that coordinate as a bit flip, and associate Pω and Pω^(i) to the endpoints. Mark the pairwise testing-error lower bound 1−v. State visually that the square illustrates the general d-dimensional hypercube argument; do not imply the theorem assumes d=2 or that a single highlighted edge alone proves the averaged bound.
editorial_candidates.limitation: Optional explanatory schematic; the written proof supplies the full averaging argument and no diagram is needed for validity.

editorial_candidates.kind: local B-spline support and partition-of-unity schematic
editorial_candidates.source_claim: On each nonempty knot interval [ξ_m,ξ_{m+1}), the p+1 active B-splines B_{m−p,p,ξ},…,B_{m,p,ξ} form a basis and sum to one; each has support [ξ_j,ξ_{j+p+1}], with continuity determined by knot multiplicity (lines 22 and 36–48).
editorial_candidates.why_warranted: The compact supports and changing active set across knots are spatial relationships that a local knot-axis sketch could clarify.
editorial_candidates.content_to_draw_or_check: Use a small generic knot axis with marked ordered knots and one highlighted nonempty cell [ξ_m,ξ_{m+1}). Draw only the p+1 active basis functions over that cell, label their supports [ξ_j,ξ_{j+p+1}], and indicate their sum is 1 on the cell. If a concrete low-degree example is chosen, explicitly mark it as illustrative and check the curve shapes/support endpoints for the chosen knot multiplicities. Do not suggest equally spaced knots, global smoothness at a repeated knot, or continuity when multiplicity is p+1.
editorial_candidates.limitation: Optional schematic only; the item proves the general result algebraically, and the source does not select a concrete knot vector or degree for a plot.
